nodes.name: Receive Inbound Webhook
nodes.notes: Entry point: listens for POST calls on /wf05819-job. Use the TEST url while building, switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after publishing. Watch out: While building use the TEST url; switch callers to the PRODUCTION url after you publish.

nodes.name: Compute HMAC Signature
nodes.notes: Computes the HMAC-SHA256 of the raw payload to verify the sender's signature before trusting the data.

nodes.name: Signature Valid?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.computedSignature === $json.headers['x-signature']. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Reject (HTTP 401)
nodes.notes: Sends the HTTP 401 response back to the caller — keep this fast; heavy work happens after/async. Watch out: Only works when the Webhook node's Response Mode is set to 'Using Respond to Webhook node'.

nodes.name: Map to Canonical Schema
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes jobId, kind, payload. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Acknowledge Fast (HTTP 202)
nodes.notes: Sends the HTTP 202 response back to the caller — keep this fast; heavy work happens after/async. Watch out: Only works when the Webhook node's Response Mode is set to 'Using Respond to Webhook node'.

nodes.name: Route by Event Kind
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: created, updated + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Handle 'created' → Google Sheets
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Job Tracker', matched on jobId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Handle 'updated' → Forward API
nodes.notes: POST https://api.example.com/v1/jobs — retries 3× with backoff on failure. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: API key / bearer for the target API. Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.

nodes.name: Log Unrecognized Kind
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Consolidate Handling
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per job (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Serialize Run Output (CSV)
nodes.notes: Serializes items to a CSV binary file.

nodes.name: Archive Row Snapshot
nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Job Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Park in Dead-Letter Queue
nodes.notes: Runs a parameterized SQL statement against Postgres — values are bound via queryReplacement, not string-interpolated, so it's immune to SQL injection. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Postgres connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.

# Pipe webhook payloads: Google Sheets, webhook

**Pattern:** Webhook Pipeline · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Webhook

## Overview

Fires when a webhook arrives, and covers process-orchestration work end to end across Google Sheets, Slack and PostgreSQL.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Receive Inbound Webhook
2. Compute HMAC Signature
3. Signature Valid?
4. Reject (HTTP 401)
5. Map to Canonical Schema
6. Acknowledge Fast (HTTP 202)
7. Route by Event Kind
8. Handle 'created' → Google Sheets
9. Handle 'updated' → Forward API
10. Log Unrecognized Kind
11. Consolidate Handling
12. Fingerprint for Idempotency
13. Drop Already-Processed Items
14. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
15. Archive Row Snapshot
16. Enrich with Reference Data
17. Fold In Enrichment Fields
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing process-orchestration work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Receive Inbound Webhook → Compute HMAC Signature → Signature Valid? → Reject (HTTP 401) → Map to Canonical Schema → Acknowledge Fast (HTTP 202) → Route by Event Kind → Handle 'created' → Google Sheets → Handle 'updated' → Forward API → Log Unrecognized Kind → Consolidate Handling → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Enrich with Reference Data → Fold In Enrichment Fields → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Google Sheets and Slack aligned by hand for process orchestration
- Pushing process-orchestration events into Google Sheets and Slack the moment they land, not on the next poll
- Process orchestration work where "Compute HMAC Signature" is still a manual step before Google Sheets
- Process orchestration work that only reaches Google Sheets when a webhook arrives, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Google Sheets and Slack in step for process orchestration, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Google Sheets or Slack are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this process-orchestration build
- A failed Google Sheets or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this process-orchestration build
- Branches rejoin before Google Sheets, so a process-orchestration run reports once rather than 23 times
- Fans the same result out to PostgreSQL in the same run, for process orchestration

## Before first run
Connect credentials: API key / bearer for the target API; Google OAuth2 / service account; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

The optional HMAC check runs before any business logic touches the payload — bad signatures are rejected at the door rather than after work has already been done with untrusted data. Acking fast (HTTP 202) and doing the real work after the response is what stops the sender's webhook delivery from timing out and re-delivering the same event.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Turn on signature verification and trace what a tampered payload does at the 'Signature Valid?' gate.
2. Add a new event kind to the switch and give it its own handler.
3. Remove the fast-ack step and observe how response time changes under a slow downstream write.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**API key / bearer for the target API**
Whatever the target API issues — usually a bearer token or API key.
_Gotcha:_ Store it as a credential, never typed into the node's parameters.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**HTTP node returns 401 or 403**
Cause: Wrong or unscoped credential, or the API expects a header this request isn't sending.
Fix: Verify the key directly with curl first, then confirm the auth type matches what the API documents.

**HTTP node returns 429**
Cause: Rate limited by the provider.
Fix: Raise the wait between calls or lower the batch size. Retries already back off, but they cannot beat a hard quota.

**Webhook returns 404**
Cause: Calling the test URL when the workflow is published, or vice versa.
Fix: Test URL works only while 'Listen for test event' is armed; the production URL needs the workflow published.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.

The HTTP node sends a secret: keep it in a header credential, never in the URL — query strings land in proxy and execution logs.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole process-orchestration payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.

The webhook path is unguessable but it is not authentication: add header auth or an IP allow-list before this endpoint is reachable from the internet.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your process orchestration process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.
